title: Booking a Restaurant Table by Phone
situation: You call a restaurant to reserve a table for dinner on the weekend.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 네, OO식당입니다. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
lines.en: Hello, this is OO Restaurant. How can I help you?
lines.note: Shops answer the phone with 네, [가게 이름]입니다 = 'Yes, this is [shop name]'

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 예약하려고 전화드렸어요.
lines.en: Hi, I'm calling to make a reservation.
lines.note: 전화드렸어요 = humble 'I called'; -(으)려고 = in order to

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 네, 언제로 예약해 드릴까요?
lines.en: Sure, for when would you like the reservation?
lines.note: 언제로 = for when; 예약해 드릴까요 = shall I book it for you?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 이번 주 토요일 저녁 일곱 시요.
lines.en: This Saturday at 7 p.m.
lines.note: 저녁 일곱 시 = 7 in the evening; trailing 요 makes a short answer polite

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 몇 분이세요?
lines.en: How many people?
lines.note: 분 = polite counter for people

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 네 명이요. 혹시 창가 자리 돼요?
lines.en: Four people. Could we possibly get a window seat?
lines.note: 혹시 = by any chance; 자리 돼요? = is a seat available?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 잠시만요… 네, 일곱 시에 창가 자리 가능해요.
lines.en: One moment… yes, a window seat is available at seven.
lines.note: 잠시만요 = just a moment; 가능해요 = it's possible/available

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 다행이다. 그럼 그걸로 할게요.
lines.en: Oh good. Then I'll take that.
lines.note: 다행이다 = 'what a relief', said to oneself; 그걸로 할게요 = I'll go with that

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 예약자 성함하고 연락처 말씀해 주시겠어요?
lines.en: Could you give me the name and phone number for the reservation?
lines.note: 예약자 성함 = name under the booking; 연락처 = contact number

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 이름은 김민수, 번호는 010-1234-5678이에요.
lines.en: The name is Kim Minsu, and the number is 010-1234-5678.
lines.note: Korean phone numbers start with 010; read digits one by one

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 확인했습니다. 토요일 일곱 시, 네 분 예약됐어요.
lines.en: Confirmed. Your reservation is for Saturday at seven, four people.
lines.note: 예약됐어요 = it's been booked (passive of 예약하다)

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 감사합니다. 그날 뵐게요.
lines.en: Thank you. See you that day.
lines.note: 그날 뵐게요 = 'I'll see you that day' (뵙다 = humble 'to see/meet')

tip: Popular restaurants fill up on weekends, so call ahead. Many places now take bookings through apps like 캐치테이블 (CatchTable) or 네이버 예약, but a quick phone call still works everywhere. If you can't make it, call to cancel — some places charge a 노쇼 (no-show) fee.

title: Describing Your Symptoms to the Doctor
situation: You see the doctor at a clinic and explain that you've had a fever, sore throat, and body aches.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 어디가 불편해서 오셨어요?
lines.en: Hello. What brings you in today?
lines.note: 어디가 불편해서 오셨어요? = the standard way a doctor asks what's wrong (불편하다 = to be uncomfortable)

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.ko: 이틀 전부터 열이 나고 목이 너무 아파요.
lines.en: I've had a fever since two days ago and my throat hurts a lot.
lines.note: 이틀 전부터 = since two days ago; 열이 나다 = to run a fever

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.ko: 기침이나 콧물도 있으세요?
lines.en: Do you also have a cough or runny nose?
lines.note: 기침 = cough; 콧물 = runny nose; -(이)나 lists options

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.ko: 기침이 좀 나고, 몸살도 있는 것 같아요.
lines.en: I have a bit of a cough, and I think I have body aches too.
lines.note: 몸살 = body aches/fatigue from being sick; -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 = it seems that ~

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.ko: 한번 열 좀 재 볼게요. 입 벌리고 '아' 해 보세요.
lines.en: Let me take your temperature. Open your mouth and say 'ah'.
lines.note: 열을 재다 = to take a temperature; 입 벌리다 = to open one's mouth

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.ko: 아… 침 삼킬 때 목이 많이 따가워요.
lines.en: Ahh… my throat really stings when I swallow.
lines.note: 침 삼키다 = to swallow (saliva); 따갑다 = to sting/be sore

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.ko: 목이 많이 부었네요. 독감 검사 한번 해 볼게요.
lines.en: Your throat is quite swollen. Let's run a flu test.
lines.note: 붓다 = to swell (부었네요 = it's swollen); 독감 검사 = flu test

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.ko: 독감이에요? 약 먹으면 금방 나아요?
lines.en: Is it the flu? Will I get better soon if I take medicine?
lines.note: 낫다 = to get better (나아요 = irregular conjugation); 금방 = soon

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.ko: 네, 약 잘 드시고 푹 쉬면 며칠 안에 나아요.
lines.en: Yes, if you take your medicine and rest well, you'll recover within a few days.
lines.note: 푹 쉬다 = to rest well; 며칠 안에 = within a few days

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.ko: 회사는 며칠 쉬는 게 좋을까요?
lines.en: How many days should I take off work?
lines.note: -는 게 좋을까요 = would it be good to ~? (asking for advice)

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.ko: 이삼 일은 쉬세요. 처방전 드릴 테니까 근처 약국에서 약 받으세요.
lines.en: Take two or three days off. I'll give you a prescription, so pick up the medicine at a nearby pharmacy.
lines.note: 이삼 일 = two or three days; 처방전 = prescription; 근처 약국 = nearby pharmacy

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.ko: 네, 알겠습니다. 진단서도 한 장 부탁드려요.
lines.en: Okay, got it. Please write me a medical certificate as well.
lines.note: 진단서 = doctor's note/medical certificate; 한 장 = one sheet; 부탁드려요 = I'd like to ask for ~

tip: Tell the doctor when it started (이틀 전부터) and your main 증상 (symptoms) — 열이 나요, 목이 아파요, 기침이 나요. The doctor gives you a 처방전 (prescription), which you take to any nearby 약국. If you need time off work, ask for a 진단서 (medical certificate); some workplaces require one.
